steps.title: Fix dissected aortas
steps.instruction: Immerse each dissected aorta in either 4 % paraformaldehyde or 10 % neutrally buffered formalin for 24–48 hours.

steps.title: Store fixed aortas in saline
steps.instruction: After fixation, transfer aortas to saline and keep at either room temperature or 2–8 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Clean aorta and remove adventitia
steps.instruction: Let the aorta sit in saline for a few hours to facilitate cleaning, then gently remove all adventitial tissue while keeping the tissue moist with saline and avoiding tears to the innominate artery, left common carotid artery, and left subclavian artery.

substeps.instruction: Leave 1 mm of the innominate and left common carotid arteries intact; cut off the entire left subclavian artery.

steps.title: Open aorta along curvatures
steps.instruction: Cut open the outer curvature sequentially through the innominate artery, then the left common carotid artery, and finally the left subclavian artery; then cut open along the inner curvature from the ascending portion to the bottom of the abdominal portion.

steps.title: Pin aorta flat on wax
steps.instruction: Place the opened aorta on black wax and pin it flat using Fine Science Tools pins (item #26002-20), keep the tissue moist with saline, label the mouse number on the wax box, and store at 4 °C. Complete imaging and analysis within 3 days of pinning.

steps.title: Capture en face images
steps.instruction: Photograph each pinned aorta with a Nikon digital camera, including a millimeter ruler in each frame for calibration. Acquire three separate images covering the Arch Region (junction of myocardium to 3 mm distal of the left subclavian artery), Thoracic Region (3 mm distal of the left subclavian artery to the last intercostal artery), and Abdominal Region (last intercostal artery to the iliac bifurcation). Save images as JPEG or TIFF files.

steps.title: Calibrate image scale in Image Pro
steps.instruction: Open the image in Image Pro (version 5.0 or 7.0). Choose Measure → Calibrate → Spatial Calibration, start a new calibration, draw a line over the ruler, set reference units to millimeters, click OK, then Apply.

steps.title: Annotate images with study information
steps.instruction: In Image Pro, click the annotation button (O), select “Aa”, click the image, enter study name, mouse number, and date, confirm with OK, then burn the label by pressing the double‑arrow (bb) button and save the annotated image. Repeat for all remaining images.

steps.title: Define regions and trace lesions
steps.instruction: For each image, select the appropriate calibration (Measure → Calibration → Set System → Apply). Use the line tool to measure 3 mm on the ruler, then:

substeps.instruction: Drag the line so one end touches the root of the left subclavian artery to mark the Arch Region.
Select the polygon tool (‑) and trace the intimal (lesion) area of the Arch Region.
Measure approximately 17 mm from the end of the Arch Region to the last intercostal artery; outline this segment as the Thoracic Region and trace its lesions.
Outline the Abdominal Region from the end of the Thoracic Region to the iliac bifurcation (optionally include 1 mm of both iliac arteries) and trace its lesions.
Inspect the aorta through the microscope while tracing to ensure accurate lesion boundaries.

steps.title: Export measurements and save files
steps.instruction: Open Input/Output, select Measurements, click “Export Now”, paste the exported data into a spreadsheet, then in Input/Output save the image as “mouse#_xxxx.msr”. Print the image with overlay if desired, and keep the image open until it has been printed, saved, and all measurements recorded in the spreadsheet.
